specs/SIGNAL_SPEC.md is frozen and authoritative for the op vocabulary, validator rule set, and lifecycle states.

SignalSpec persistence (one row per version plus YAML body) is satisfied via a QuestDB signal_specs table with a Redis signals:catalog hot-view cache; no new OLTP (Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, Drizzle) layer is permitted.

compose-stack regression harness from R-009 is available for Playwright fixture serving.

critic.rationale: The plan is architecturally sound and well-structured. The design_contract provides explicit persistence_protocol (QuestDB signal_specs DDL with lifecycle enum, unique-PROMOTED constraint, Redis hot-view invalidation) and concurrency_protocol (lifecycle-state CAS, 409 Conflict, DB-level unique constraint). All six slices have non-overlapping allowed/forbidden paths; QA paths are fully disjoint from implementer source paths. The split_specialists topology is consistent with two specialist implementer slices. All implementer and QA slices carry verification commands. The dependency chain design→qa-author→impl-primary→impl-ui→review→qa-verify is correctly ordered with no orphan slices, a reviewer is present, finalization is human-gated, the risk register covers 12 named risks with mitigations, and the R-015 prerequisite is explicitly sequenced as a preflight gate. The one confirmed gap — flagged by the validator error — is check_lifecycle_coverage: the acceptance_test_matrix and acceptance_tests array do not include a stale/invalid test for the Redis signals:catalog hot-view (R11 in the risk register acknowledges the staleness risk and mandates synchronous invalidation, but no acceptance criterion verifies that a promote or archive call immediately yields fresh catalog data). The invariant-failure-on-read and backtest-failure/partial-state cases are both covered, but the stale-cache branch is not exercised by any named test.

critic.rationale: The R-016 plan is structurally sound across all 17 rubric dimensions. The design_contract carries fully specified persistence (QuestDB signal_specs DDL, lifecycle state machine, Redis hot-view, YAML re-validation on read) and concurrency (optimistic CAS BACKTESTED→PROMOTED, unique-PROMOTED DB constraint, 409 Conflict) protocols. Every affected surface maps to at least one slice's allowed_paths and is exercised by tests. No slice has intra-slice allowed/forbidden overlap. All implementer and QA slices carry concrete verification commands (Gradle and npm). Lifecycle coverage spans stale/invalid (synchronous Redis invalidation post-promote and post-archive), invariant (re-validate YAML on read with structured error), and failure/partial (backtest failure leaves COMPILED state; same proposalId retryable). split_specialists topology is compatible with the two implementer slices. The slice chain design→qa-author→impl-primary→impl-ui→review→qa-verify has no orphans; review is present; qa-author precedes implementers; qa-verify follows review. QA allowed paths (tests/, qa/fixtures/, app-api/src/test/, ui/tests/) are fully disjoint from implementer allowed paths (platform-dsl/, app-api/src/main/, ui/src/). The finalization policy locks final PR merge to a human operator. Objectives name concrete files and test classes throughout. A 12-entry risk register is present with HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW ratings and explicit mitigations. The R-015 prerequisite is explicitly sequenced via assumption, Risk R1, and design-slice preflight gate. No work touches JMH-benchmarked hot-path nodes; hard constraints forbid BacktestRunner duplication and new OLTP introduction. R-016 is a multi-surface complex feature (new DSL module, 5 REST endpoints, persistence layer, 2 UI pages, Redis cache, full lifecycle state machine); 6 slices is appropriate and the small-feature compactness check does not apply.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Promotion endpoint uses optimistic lock / lifecycle state CAS on the signal_specs row (BACKTESTED → PROMOTED). Concurrent promote requests for the same signalId are serialized at the persistence layer; the second concurrent caller receives 409 Conflict with the current lifecycle_state in the response body. The unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') provides a DB-level safety net against double-promotion.
forbidden_alternatives: Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle as an OLTP layer for SignalSpec storage.
Wiring any auto-promotion path that bypasses operator confirmation.
Generating Java signal classes from SignalSpec YAML (v2 scope only).
Patching dag_framework locally without upstreaming first.
Serving SignalSpec compilation results directly from the UI without routing through app-api.
Forking or duplicating R-015 BacktestRunner backtest execution logic.
Storing signal YAML only in Redis without QuestDB durability.
Returning raw yaml_body in the catalog listing endpoint (metadata and status only).
Using SnakeYAML UnsafeConstructor or any equivalent unsafe YAML deserialization path.
Deferring Redis signals:catalog invalidation to a background thread or async event after the HTTP response is returned.
hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals (deferred to v2); compiler output is an in-memory FeatureNodeGraph only.
Auto-promotion without explicit operator confirmation token is forbidden at both API and UI layers; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote must return 403 without a valid token.
Reuse R-015 POST /api/backtest/run for signal backtesting; do not duplicate or fork replay logic.
app-api must not introduce a new OLTP database; persistence is QuestDB signal_specs table plus Redis hot-view only.
platform-dsl/signalspec/ must not import app-api or app-core classes; only platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs.
UI-facing API contract changes must update docs/UI_API_CONTRACT_PROVENANCE_MATRIX.md and docs/UI_BACKEND_CONTRACT_GAP_HANDOFF.md.
SignalSpecValidator must use SnakeYAML SafeConstructor exclusively; no UnsafeConstructor usage permitted.
Any new app-api write path requires a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry before implementation begins.
Redis signals:catalog hot-view must be invalidated synchronously within the same request scope as any promote or archive state mutation; async or lazy invalidation is forbidden.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl/signalspec/ owns SignalSpecValidator and SignalSpecCompiler; it depends on platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs only and must not import app-api or app-core domain objects. app-api owns REST endpoints, SignalSpecRepository (QuestDB signal_specs persistence), Redis catalog hot-view, and explainability envelope extension. ui/ owns SignalsCatalog view and SignalReview page with promote/archive buttons gated on operator confirmation modal. dag_framework and platform-runtime FeatureNode primitives are consumed not extended. repo-memory/DECISIONS.md must gain a write-path authorization entry from the design slice before impl-primary begins.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: One row per SignalSpec version in a signal_specs table: id UUID PK, apiVersion TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version INT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, lifecycle_state TEXT CHECK IN ('PROPOSED','VALIDATED','COMPILED','BACKTESTED','PROMOTED','ARCHIVED') NOT NULL, yaml_body TEXT NOT NULL, proposalId UUID NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP, promoted_at TIMESTAMP, backtest_summary_json TEXT; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state) where lifecycle_state='PROMOTED' enforces single-promotion invariant. Lifecycle state machine: PROPOSED → VALIDATED → COMPILED → BACKTESTED → (PROMOTED | ARCHIVED). YAML body is stored verbatim and re-validated on read to detect invariant failures; GET /api/signals/{id} returns a structured invariant-failure error (not 500) if re-validation fails. Redis key signals:catalog caches PROPOSED+PROMOTED listing; invalidated synchronously on every promote or archive call before the HTTP response is returned — no stale entry may be served to a caller that issues GET /api/signals/catalog after a successful state-mutation response.

final.problem_statement: There is no declarative signal authoring surface: LLM-proposed SignalSpecs cannot be validated, compiled to FeatureNode graphs, backtested, reviewed, or promoted to live ranking with operator approval and author provenance. The platform cannot close the propose→validate→compile→backtest→promote loop required to make R-016 acceptance criteria reachable.

design_contract.persistence_protocol: One row per SignalSpec version in a signal_specs table: id UUID PK, apiVersion TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version INT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, lifecycle_state TEXT CHECK IN ('PROPOSED','VALIDATED','COMPILED','BACKTESTED','PROMOTED','ARCHIVED') NOT NULL, yaml_body TEXT NOT NULL, proposalId UUID NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP, promoted_at TIMESTAMP, backtest_summary_json TEXT; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state) where lifecycle_state='PROMOTED' enforces single-promotion invariant. Lifecycle state machine: PROPOSED → VALIDATED → COMPILED → BACKTESTED → (PROMOTED | ARCHIVED). YAML body is stored verbatim and re-validated on read to detect invariant failures; GET /api/signals/{id} returns a structured invariant-failure error (not 500) if re-validation fails. Redis key signals:catalog caches PROPOSED+PROMOTED listing; invalidated synchronously on every promote or archive call. QuestDB is the canonical durable store; Redis is the hot-view cache only. No Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle may be introduced.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Promotion endpoint is idempotent and guarded by a compare-and-swap on lifecycle state (PROPOSED -> LIVE). Concurrent promote requests for the same signalId must be serialized at the Redis/QuestDB write layer; the second concurrent caller receives 409 Conflict with the current lifecycle state in the response body.
forbidden_alternatives: Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle as an OLTP layer for SignalSpec storage.
Wiring any auto-promotion path that bypasses operator confirmation.
Generating Java signal classes from SignalSpec YAML (v2 scope only).
Patching dag_framework locally without upstreaming first.
Serving SignalSpec compilation results directly from the UI without routing through app-api.
hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals (deferred to v2).
Auto-promotion without explicit operator confirmation token is forbidden at both API and UI layers.
Reuse R-015 POST /api/backtest/run path for signal backtesting; do not duplicate replay logic.
app-api must not introduce a new OLTP database; persistence is Redis hot views or QuestDB historical store only.
platform-dsl/signalspec/ must not import app-api or app-core classes; only platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs.
UI-facing API contract changes must update docs/UI_API_CONTRACT_PROVENANCE_MATRIX.md and docs/UI_BACKEND_CONTRACT_GAP_HANDOFF.md.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl/signalspec/ owns validator and compiler only; it depends on platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs and must not import app-api or app-core domain objects. app-api owns REST endpoints, persistence projection (Redis catalog hash or QuestDB signals_catalog via existing historical-store seam), and provenance envelope extension. ui/ owns SignalsCatalog view and SignalReview page with promote/archive buttons gated on operator confirmation. dag_framework is read-only from this feature's perspective.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: One logical row per SignalSpec (signalId, version, author, lifecycle, proposalId, trackRecord JSON) plus raw YAML body stored as a Redis hash (signal:catalog:<signalId>) or QuestDB signals_catalog table — choice locked in design slice. No new OLTP database. app-api must not write directly to persistence; writes flow through app-core projections or the existing historical-store bulk-loader seam consistent with the Redis-hot-view/historical-store-canonical-split decision.
design_contract.public_api: SignalSpecValidator.validate(SignalSpec): ValidationResult with per-diagnostic file/line/message; SignalSpecCompiler.compile(ValidatedSpec): FeatureNodeGraph targeting existing platform-runtime FeatureNode primitives. REST: POST /api/signals/propose, GET /api/signals/catalog, GET /api/signals/{id}, POST /api/signals/{id}/promote (returns 403 without operator token; 409 on concurrent promote), POST /api/signals/{id}/archive. Explainability envelope DTO extended with: author, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, trackRecord.

candidate.problem_statement: There is no declarative signal authoring surface: LLM-proposed SignalSpecs cannot be validated, compiled to FeatureNode graphs, backtested, reviewed, or promoted to live ranking with operator approval and author provenance. The platform cannot close the propose->validate->compile->backtest->promote loop required to make R-016 acceptance criteria reachable.
risk_register: R1 (HIGH): SignalSpec persistence may conflict with the Redis+historical-store-only architecture decision — mitigation: design slice must resolve storage mechanism (Redis catalog hash vs new QuestDB signals_catalog table with schema migration file) before impl-dsl-backend begins; any QuestDB table requires a DDL migration consistent with questdb/schema_bootstrap.sql.

R2 (MEDIUM): platform-dsl/signalspec/ may inadvertently import app-api or app-core classes — mitigation: reviewer import-boundary checklist is a required output of the review slice; compile-time module boundaries should be enforced via build.gradle dependency declarations.

R3 (MEDIUM): Concurrent promote race condition — mitigation: compare-and-swap at persistence layer; 409 response wired in SignalController; acceptance test for concurrent promote is a required output in qa-author.

R4 (HIGH): R-015 backtest path not merged when R-016 impl starts — mitigation: assumption asserted in design contract; IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT_TRACK_A_CONTINUATION.yaml preflight gate must be honored; impl-dsl-backend must not begin until R-015 is confirmed on main.

R5 (MEDIUM): Operator confirmation token bypassable client-side — mitigation: backend always validates token server-side returning 403; SignalApiEndpointTest.java covers missing-token case; reviewer checks UI does not skip token injection.

R6 (LOW): Cycle detection in SignalSpecValidator may miss indirect cycles — mitigation: qa/fixtures/signalspec/invalid-cyclic-transform.yaml must encode a 3-node indirect cycle (A->B->C->A); reviewer explicitly checks DFS covers all transform edge reachability.

hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals — declarative SignalSpec YAML is the only v1 authoring surface.
Do not allow auto-promotion: POST /api/signals/{id}/promote must require an explicit operator confirmation token and return 403 without it.
Reuse R-015 POST /api/backtest/run for the backtest step; do not introduce a parallel backtest execution path.

design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl/signalspec/ owns SignalSpecValidator and SignalSpecCompiler targeting FeatureNode primitives in platform-runtime (read-only dependency, no FeatureNode modification); app-api owns HTTP controllers, signal_specs persistence, and explainability envelope projection; ui/ owns the Signal Catalog page and detail view; platform-runtime FeatureNode primitives are consumed not extended.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: One row per SignalSpec version in signal_specs table: id (UUID PK), apiVersion, name, version, author, lifecycle_state ENUM, yaml_body TEXT, created_at, promoted_at; lifecycle state machine: PROPOSED → VALIDATED → COMPILED → BACKTESTED → (PROMOTED | ARCHIVED); YAML body is stored verbatim and re-validated on read to detect invariant failures.
design_contract.public_api: SignalSpec v1 YAML schema as defined in specs/SIGNAL_SPEC.md; POST /api/signals/propose (accepts YAML body, returns proposalId + structured validation diagnostics); GET /api/signals/catalog (paginated, filterable by lifecycle state, includes author and trackRecord); GET /api/signals/{id} (full spec + track record); POST /api/signals/{id}/promote (requires explicit operator confirmation token, transitions BACKTESTED→PROMOTED only); POST /api/signals/{id}/archive (transitions any non-PROMOTED state to ARCHIVED); Phase 1 explainability envelope extended with author, signalId, signalVersion, proposalId, trackRecord on opportunity and cockpit responses.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Promotion endpoint uses optimistic lock / lifecycle state CAS on the signal_specs row (BACKTESTED → PROMOTED). Concurrent promote requests for the same signalId are serialized at the persistence layer; the second concurrent caller receives 409 Conflict with the current lifecycle_state in the response body. The unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') provides a DB-level safety net against double-promotion.
forbidden_alternatives: Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle as an OLTP layer for SignalSpec storage.
Wiring any auto-promotion path that bypasses operator confirmation.
Generating Java signal classes from SignalSpec YAML (v2 scope only).
Patching dag_framework locally without upstreaming first.
Serving SignalSpec compilation results directly from the UI without routing through app-api.
Forking or duplicating R-015 BacktestRunner backtest execution logic.
Storing signal YAML only in Redis without QuestDB durability.
Returning raw yaml_body in the catalog listing endpoint (metadata and status only).
Using SnakeYAML UnsafeConstructor or any equivalent unsafe YAML deserialization path.
Deferring Redis signals:catalog invalidation to a background thread or async event after the HTTP response is returned.
hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals (deferred to v2); compiler output is an in-memory FeatureNodeGraph only.
Auto-promotion without explicit operator confirmation token is forbidden at both API and UI layers; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote must return 403 without a valid token.
Reuse R-015 POST /api/backtest/run for signal backtesting; do not duplicate or fork replay logic.
app-api must not introduce a new OLTP database; persistence is QuestDB signal_specs table plus Redis hot-view only.
platform-dsl/signalspec/ must not import app-api or app-core classes; only platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs.
UI-facing API contract changes must update docs/UI_API_CONTRACT_PROVENANCE_MATRIX.md and docs/UI_BACKEND_CONTRACT_GAP_HANDOFF.md.
SignalSpecValidator must use SnakeYAML SafeConstructor exclusively; no UnsafeConstructor usage permitted.
Any new app-api write path requires a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry before implementation begins.
Redis signals:catalog hot-view must be invalidated synchronously within the same request scope as any promote or archive state mutation; async or lazy invalidation is forbidden.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl/signalspec/ owns SignalSpecValidator and SignalSpecCompiler; it depends on platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs only and must not import app-api or app-core domain objects. app-api owns REST endpoints, SignalSpecRepository (QuestDB signal_specs persistence), Redis catalog hot-view, and explainability envelope extension. ui/ owns SignalsCatalog view and SignalReview page with promote/archive buttons gated on operator confirmation modal. dag_framework and platform-runtime FeatureNode primitives are consumed not extended. repo-memory/DECISIONS.md must gain a write-path authorization entry from the design slice before impl-primary begins.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: One row per SignalSpec version in a signal_specs table: id UUID PK, apiVersion TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version INT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, lifecycle_state TEXT CHECK IN ('PROPOSED','VALIDATED','COMPILED','BACKTESTED','PROMOTED','ARCHIVED') NOT NULL, yaml_body TEXT NOT NULL, proposalId UUID NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP, promoted_at TIMESTAMP, backtest_summary_json TEXT; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state) where lifecycle_state='PROMOTED' enforces single-promotion invariant. Lifecycle state machine: PROPOSED → VALIDATED → COMPILED → BACKTESTED → (PROMOTED | ARCHIVED). YAML body is stored verbatim and re-validated on read to detect invariant failures; GET /api/signals/{id} returns a structured invariant-failure error (not 500) if re-validation fails. Redis key signals:catalog caches PROPOSED+PROMOTED listing; invalidated synchronously on every promote or archive call before the HTTP response is returned — no stale entry may be served to a caller that issues GET /api/signals/catalog after a successful state-mutation response.
design_contract.public_api: SignalSpecValidator.validate(String yaml): ValidationResult{ok, diagnostics[{fieldPath, errorCode, message, suggestion, file, line}]}; SignalSpecCompiler.compile(ValidatedSpec): FeatureNodeGraph (in-memory only, no Java codegen). REST: POST /api/signals/propose (body: SignalSpec YAML) → ProposalResponse{proposalId, signalId, validationResult}; GET /api/signals/catalog (paginated, filterable by lifecycle_state) → SignalCatalogEntry[]{signalId, author, lifecycle_state, trackRecord}; GET /api/signals/{id} → SignalSpecDetail{full spec + diagnostics + trackRecord}; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote (operator confirmation token required; returns 403 without valid token; returns 422 if signal not in BACKTESTED state; returns 409 on concurrent promote for same signalId) → PromoteResponse; POST /api/signals/{id}/archive → ArchiveResponse. Explainability envelope DTO extended with: author (String), signalId (UUID), signalVersion (int), proposalId (UUID), trackRecord (TrackRecordSummary).

consolidated.problem_statement: There is no declarative signal authoring surface: LLM-proposed SignalSpecs cannot be validated, compiled to FeatureNode graphs, backtested, reviewed, or promoted to live ranking with operator approval and author provenance. The platform cannot close the propose→validate→compile→backtest→promote loop required to make R-016 acceptance criteria reachable.

critic.rationale: The R-016 plan is structurally sound across all 17 rubric dimensions. The design_contract carries fully specified persistence (QuestDB signal_specs DDL, lifecycle state machine, Redis hot-view, YAML re-validation on read) and concurrency (optimistic CAS BACKTESTED→PROMOTED, unique-PROMOTED DB constraint, 409 Conflict) protocols. R-016 is a multi-surface complex feature (new DSL module, 5 REST endpoints, persistence layer, 2 UI pages, Redis cache, full lifecycle state machine); 6 slices is appropriate and the small-feature compactness check does not apply.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Promotion endpoint uses optimistic lock / lifecycle state CAS on the signal_specs row (BACKTESTED → PROMOTED). Concurrent promote requests for the same signalId are serialized at the persistence layer; the second concurrent caller receives 409 Conflict with the current lifecycle_state in the response body. The unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') provides a DB-level safety net against double-promotion.
forbidden_alternatives: Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle as an OLTP layer for SignalSpec storage.
Wiring any auto-promotion path that bypasses operator confirmation.
Generating Java signal classes from SignalSpec YAML (v2 scope only).
Patching dag_framework locally without upstreaming first.
Serving SignalSpec compilation results directly from the UI without routing through app-api.
Forking or duplicating R-015 BacktestRunner backtest execution logic.
Storing signal YAML only in Redis without QuestDB durability.
Returning raw yaml_body in the catalog listing endpoint (metadata and status only).
Using SnakeYAML UnsafeConstructor or any equivalent unsafe YAML deserialization path.
Deferring Redis signals:catalog invalidation to a background thread or async event after the HTTP response is returned.
hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals (deferred to v2); compiler output is an in-memory FeatureNodeGraph only.
Auto-promotion without explicit operator confirmation token is forbidden at both API and UI layers; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote must return 403 without a valid token.
Reuse R-015 POST /api/backtest/run for signal backtesting; do not duplicate or fork replay logic.
app-api must not introduce a new OLTP database; persistence is QuestDB signal_specs table plus Redis hot-view only.
platform-dsl/signalspec/ must not import app-api or app-core classes; only platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs.
UI-facing API contract changes must update docs/UI_API_CONTRACT_PROVENANCE_MATRIX.md and docs/UI_BACKEND_CONTRACT_GAP_HANDOFF.md.
SignalSpecValidator must use SnakeYAML SafeConstructor exclusively; no UnsafeConstructor usage permitted.
Any new app-api write path requires a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry before implementation begins.
Redis signals:catalog hot-view must be invalidated synchronously within the same request scope as any promote or archive state mutation; async or lazy invalidation is forbidden.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl/signalspec/ owns SignalSpecValidator and SignalSpecCompiler; it depends on platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs only and must not import app-api or app-core domain objects. app-api owns REST endpoints, SignalSpecRepository (QuestDB signal_specs persistence), Redis catalog hot-view, and explainability envelope extension. ui/ owns SignalsCatalog view and SignalReview page with promote/archive buttons gated on operator confirmation modal. dag_framework and platform-runtime FeatureNode primitives are consumed not extended. repo-memory/DECISIONS.md must gain a write-path authorization entry from the design slice before impl-primary begins.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: One row per SignalSpec version in a signal_specs table: id UUID PK, apiVersion TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version INT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, lifecycle_state TEXT CHECK IN ('PROPOSED','VALIDATED','COMPILED','BACKTESTED','PROMOTED','ARCHIVED') NOT NULL, yaml_body TEXT NOT NULL, proposalId UUID NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP, promoted_at TIMESTAMP, backtest_summary_json TEXT; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state) where lifecycle_state='PROMOTED' enforces single-promotion invariant. Lifecycle state machine: PROPOSED → VALIDATED → COMPILED → BACKTESTED → (PROMOTED | ARCHIVED). YAML body is stored verbatim and re-validated on read to detect invariant failures; GET /api/signals/{id} returns a structured invariant-failure error (not 500) if re-validation fails. Redis key signals:catalog caches PROPOSED+PROMOTED listing; invalidated synchronously on every promote or archive call before the HTTP response is returned — no stale entry may be served to a caller that issues GET /api/signals/catalog after a successful state-mutation response.
design_contract.public_api: SignalSpecValidator.validate(String yaml): ValidationResult{ok, diagnostics[{fieldPath, errorCode, message, suggestion, file, line}]}; SignalSpecCompiler.compile(ValidatedSpec): FeatureNodeGraph (in-memory only, no Java codegen). REST: POST /api/signals/propose (body: SignalSpec YAML) → ProposalResponse{proposalId, signalId, validationResult}; GET /api/signals/catalog (paginated, filterable by lifecycle_state) → SignalCatalogEntry[]{signalId, author, lifecycle_state, trackRecord}; GET /api/signals/{id} → SignalSpecDetail{full spec + diagnostics + trackRecord}; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote (operator confirmation token required; returns 403 without valid token; returns 422 if signal not in BACKTESTED state; returns 409 on concurrent promote for same signalId) → PromoteResponse; POST /api/signals/{id}/archive → ArchiveResponse. Explainability envelope DTO extended with: author (String), signalId (UUID), signalVersion (int), proposalId (UUID), trackRecord (TrackRecordSummary).

candidate.problem_statement: There is no declarative signal authoring surface: LLM-proposed SignalSpecs cannot be validated, compiled to FeatureNode graphs, backtested, reviewed, or promoted to live ranking with operator approval and author provenance. The platform cannot close the propose→validate→compile→backtest→promote loop required to make R-016 acceptance criteria reachable.
risk_register: R1 (HIGH): R-015 POST /api/backtest/run not confirmed on main when R-016 impl starts — mitigation: design slice asserts R-015 preflight; impl-primary must not begin until R-015 is confirmed on main.

R2 (HIGH): SignalSpec persistence write path conflicts with Redis+historical-store-only architecture decision — mitigation: design slice adds a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry for the QuestDB signal_specs write path before impl-primary begins; reviewer verifies entry exists.

R3 (MEDIUM): platform-dsl/signalspec/ may inadvertently import app-api or app-core classes — mitigation: reviewer import-boundary checklist is a required output of the review slice; build.gradle dependency declarations enforce compile-time module boundaries.

R4 (MEDIUM): Concurrent promote race condition producing duplicate PROMOTED rows — mitigation: lifecycle state CAS at persistence layer; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') in DDL migration; 409 response wired in SignalController; qa-author includes concurrent-promote test asserting 409.

R5 (MEDIUM): Operator confirmation token bypassable client-side — mitigation: backend always validates token server-side returning 403; SignalApiEndpointTest covers missing-token case before impl-primary lands; reviewer audits Spring Security role annotation and UI confirm-modal wiring.

R6 (MEDIUM): DFS cycle detection may miss indirect cycles of 3+ hops — mitigation: qa-author writes self-ref, 2-hop, and 3-hop cycle fixture cases before impl-primary; reviewer explicitly checks DFS reachability across all transform edges.

R7 (MEDIUM): YAML body stored without re-validation may diverge from validator rules after future schema change — mitigation: re-validate YAML on read per persistence_protocol; GET /api/signals/{id} returns structured invariant-failure error rather than 500; qa-author includes invariant-failure-on-read test case.
R8 (MEDIUM): Explainability envelope extension may break existing api-contract-snapshots tests — mitigation: qa-author updates snapshot fixtures to include new fields before impl-primary lands.

R9 (MEDIUM): specs/SIGNAL_SPEC.md op vocabulary ambiguity in cyclic-transform detection and unknown-ref scoping — mitigation: designer slice resolves all ambiguities in writing and locks the diagnostic schema before qa-author proceeds.
R10 (LOW): YAML injection risk from unsafe YAML constructor — mitigation: SignalSpecValidator must use SnakeYAML SafeConstructor exclusively; reviewer checks for any UnsafeConstructor usage.

R11 (MEDIUM): Redis signals:catalog staleness after promote or archive — mitigation: synchronous Redis key invalidation within the same request scope before HTTP response is returned; async or lazy invalidation path is forbidden by hard_constraints; SignalCatalogStaleTest in qa-author asserts both post-promote and post-archive freshness transitions before impl-primary begins; reviewer explicitly verifies no async invalidation path in SignalService.

R12 (LOW): signal_specs DDL migration absent when integration tests run — mitigation: design contract includes full DDL; impl-primary fails fast if migration file is missing rather than auto-creating tables.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Promotion endpoint uses optimistic lock / lifecycle state CAS on the signal_specs row (BACKTESTED → PROMOTED). Concurrent promote requests for the same signalId are serialized at the persistence layer; the second concurrent caller receives 409 Conflict with the current lifecycle_state in the response body. The unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') provides a DB-level safety net against double-promotion.
forbidden_alternatives: Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle as an OLTP layer for SignalSpec storage.
Wiring any auto-promotion path that bypasses operator confirmation.
Generating Java signal classes from SignalSpec YAML (v2 scope only).
Patching dag_framework locally without upstreaming first.
Serving SignalSpec compilation results directly from the UI without routing through app-api.
Forking or duplicating R-015 BacktestRunner backtest execution logic.
Storing signal YAML only in Redis without QuestDB durability.
Returning raw yaml_body in the catalog listing endpoint (metadata and status only).
Using SnakeYAML UnsafeConstructor or any equivalent unsafe YAML deserialization path.
Deferring Redis signals:catalog invalidation to a background thread or async event after the HTTP response is returned.
hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals (deferred to v2); compiler output is an in-memory FeatureNodeGraph only.
Auto-promotion without explicit operator confirmation token is forbidden at both API and UI layers; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote must return 403 without a valid token.
Reuse R-015 POST /api/backtest/run for signal backtesting; do not duplicate or fork replay logic.
app-api must not introduce a new OLTP database; persistence is QuestDB signal_specs table plus Redis hot-view only.
platform-dsl/signalspec/ must not import app-api or app-core classes; only platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs.

Any new app-api write path requires a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry before implementation begins.
Redis signals:catalog must be invalidated synchronously (before HTTP response returns) on every promote and archive call; eventual or async invalidation is forbidden.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl/signalspec/ owns SignalSpecValidator and SignalSpecCompiler; it depends on platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs only and must not import app-api or app-core domain objects. app-api owns REST endpoints, SignalSpecRepository (QuestDB signal_specs persistence), Redis catalog hot-view, and explainability envelope extension. ui/ owns SignalsCatalog view and SignalReview page with promote/archive buttons gated on operator confirmation modal. dag_framework and platform-runtime FeatureNode primitives are consumed not extended. repo-memory/DECISIONS.md must gain a write-path authorization entry from the design slice before impl-primary begins.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: One row per SignalSpec version in a signal_specs table: id UUID PK, apiVersion TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version INT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, lifecycle_state TEXT CHECK IN ('PROPOSED','VALIDATED','COMPILED','BACKTESTED','PROMOTED','ARCHIVED') NOT NULL, yaml_body TEXT NOT NULL, proposalId UUID NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP, promoted_at TIMESTAMP, backtest_summary_json TEXT; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state) where lifecycle_state='PROMOTED' enforces single-promotion invariant. Lifecycle state machine: PROPOSED → VALIDATED → COMPILED → BACKTESTED → (PROMOTED | ARCHIVED). YAML body is stored verbatim and re-validated on read to detect invariant failures; GET /api/signals/{id} returns a structured invariant-failure error (not 500) if re-validation fails. Redis key signals:catalog caches PROPOSED+PROMOTED listing; invalidated synchronously on every promote or archive call before the HTTP response is returned — no async or eventual invalidation is permitted.
design_contract.public_api: SignalSpecValidator.validate(String yaml): ValidationResult{ok, diagnostics[{fieldPath, errorCode, message, suggestion, file, line}]}; SignalSpecCompiler.compile(ValidatedSpec): FeatureNodeGraph (in-memory only, no Java codegen). REST: POST /api/signals/propose (body: SignalSpec YAML) → ProposalResponse{proposalId, signalId, validationResult}; GET /api/signals/catalog (paginated, filterable by lifecycle_state) → SignalCatalogEntry[]{signalId, author, lifecycle_state, trackRecord}; GET /api/signals/{id} → SignalSpecDetail{full spec + diagnostics + trackRecord}; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote (operator confirmation token required; returns 403 without valid token; returns 422 if signal not in BACKTESTED state; returns 409 on concurrent promote for same signalId) → PromoteResponse; POST /api/signals/{id}/archive → ArchiveResponse. Explainability envelope DTO extended with: author (String), signalId (UUID), signalVersion (int), proposalId (UUID), trackRecord (TrackRecordSummary).

candidate.problem_statement: There is no declarative signal authoring surface: LLM-proposed SignalSpecs cannot be validated, compiled to FeatureNode graphs, backtested, reviewed, or promoted to live ranking with operator approval and author provenance. The platform cannot close the propose→validate→compile→backtest→promote loop required to make R-016 acceptance criteria reachable.
risk_register: R1 (HIGH): R-015 POST /api/backtest/run not confirmed on main when R-016 impl starts — mitigation: design slice asserts R-015 preflight; impl-primary must not begin until R-015 is confirmed on main.

R2 (HIGH): SignalSpec persistence write path conflicts with Redis+historical-store-only architecture decision — mitigation: design slice adds a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry for the QuestDB signal_specs write path before impl-primary begins; reviewer verifies entry exists.

R3 (MEDIUM): platform-dsl/signalspec/ may inadvertently import app-api or app-core classes — mitigation: reviewer import-boundary checklist is a required output of the review slice; build.gradle dependency declarations enforce compile-time module boundaries.

R4 (MEDIUM): Concurrent promote race condition producing duplicate PROMOTED rows — mitigation: lifecycle state CAS at persistence layer; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') in DDL migration; 409 response wired in SignalController; qa-author includes concurrent-promote test asserting 409.

R5 (MEDIUM): Operator confirmation token bypassable client-side — mitigation: backend always validates token server-side returning 403; SignalApiEndpointTest covers missing-token case before impl-primary lands; reviewer audits Spring Security role annotation and UI confirm-modal wiring.

R6 (MEDIUM): DFS cycle detection may miss indirect cycles of 3+ hops — mitigation: qa-author writes self-ref, 2-hop, and 3-hop cycle fixture cases before impl-primary; reviewer explicitly checks DFS reachability across all transform edges.

R7 (MEDIUM): YAML body stored without re-validation may diverge from validator rules after future schema change — mitigation: re-validate YAML on read per persistence_protocol; GET /api/signals/{id} returns structured invariant-failure error rather than 500; qa-author includes invariant-failure-on-read test case.
R8 (MEDIUM): Explainability envelope extension may break existing api-contract-snapshots tests — mitigation: qa-author updates snapshot fixtures to include new fields before impl-primary lands.

R9 (MEDIUM): specs/SIGNAL_SPEC.md op vocabulary ambiguity in cyclic-transform detection and unknown-ref scoping — mitigation: designer slice resolves all ambiguities in writing and locks the diagnostic schema before qa-author proceeds.
R10 (LOW): YAML injection risk from unsafe YAML constructor — mitigation: SignalSpecValidator must use SnakeYAML SafeConstructor exclusively; reviewer checks for any UnsafeConstructor usage.

R11 (MEDIUM): Redis signals:catalog async invalidation introduces stale-read window after promote or archive — mitigation: synchronous Redis key deletion before HTTP response is committed enforced in SignalService; SignalCatalogCacheInvalidationTest asserts no stale entry visible on immediate subsequent GET; reviewer verifies no async/background invalidation path exists; stale/invalid acceptance criteria covers both promote and archive branches.

R12 (LOW): signal_specs DDL migration absent when integration tests run — mitigation: design contract includes full DDL; impl-primary fails fast if migration file is missing rather than auto-creating tables.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Promotion endpoint uses optimistic lock / lifecycle state CAS on the signal_specs row (BACKTESTED → PROMOTED). Concurrent promote requests for the same signalId are serialized at the persistence layer; the second concurrent caller receives 409 Conflict with the current lifecycle_state in the response body. The unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') provides a DB-level safety net against double-promotion.
forbidden_alternatives: Adding Postgres, SQLite, Prisma, or Drizzle as an OLTP layer for SignalSpec storage.
Wiring any auto-promotion path that bypasses operator confirmation.
Generating Java signal classes from SignalSpec YAML (v2 scope only).
Patching dag_framework locally without upstreaming first.
Serving SignalSpec compilation results directly from the UI without routing through app-api.
Forking or duplicating R-015 BacktestRunner backtest execution logic.
Storing signal YAML only in Redis without QuestDB durability.
Returning raw yaml_body in the catalog listing endpoint (metadata and status only).
Using SnakeYAML UnsafeConstructor or any equivalent unsafe YAML deserialization path.
Allowing Redis catalog TTL expiry to be the only cache-busting mechanism; synchronous invalidation is mandatory.
hard_constraints: Do not add Java code generation for signals (deferred to v2); compiler output is an in-memory FeatureNodeGraph only.
Auto-promotion without explicit operator confirmation token is forbidden at both API and UI layers; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote must return 403 without a valid token.
Reuse R-015 POST /api/backtest/run for signal backtesting; do not duplicate or fork replay logic.
app-api must not introduce a new OLTP database; persistence is QuestDB signal_specs table plus Redis hot-view only.
platform-dsl/signalspec/ must not import app-api or app-core classes; only platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs.
UI-facing API contract changes must update docs/UI_API_CONTRACT_PROVENANCE_MATRIX.md and docs/UI_BACKEND_CONTRACT_GAP_HANDOFF.md.
SignalSpecValidator must use SnakeYAML SafeConstructor exclusively; no UnsafeConstructor usage permitted.
Any new app-api write path requires a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry before implementation begins.
Redis signals:catalog must be invalidated synchronously on every promote and archive; serving stale catalog state after a state-mutating call is a contract violation.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: platform-dsl/signalspec/ owns SignalSpecValidator and SignalSpecCompiler; it depends on platform-runtime FeatureNode SPIs only and must not import app-api or app-core domain objects. app-api owns REST endpoints, SignalSpecRepository (QuestDB signal_specs persistence), Redis catalog hot-view, and explainability envelope extension. ui/ owns SignalsCatalog view and SignalReview page with promote/archive buttons gated on operator confirmation modal. dag_framework and platform-runtime FeatureNode primitives are consumed not extended. repo-memory/DECISIONS.md must gain a write-path authorization entry from the design slice before impl-primary begins.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: One row per SignalSpec version in a signal_specs table: id UUID PK, apiVersion TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version INT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, lifecycle_state TEXT CHECK IN ('PROPOSED','VALIDATED','COMPILED','BACKTESTED','PROMOTED','ARCHIVED') NOT NULL, yaml_body TEXT NOT NULL, proposalId UUID NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP, promoted_at TIMESTAMP, backtest_summary_json TEXT; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state) where lifecycle_state='PROMOTED' enforces single-promotion invariant. Lifecycle state machine: PROPOSED → VALIDATED → COMPILED → BACKTESTED → (PROMOTED | ARCHIVED). YAML body is stored verbatim and re-validated on read to detect invariant failures; GET /api/signals/{id} returns a structured invariant-failure error (not 500) if re-validation fails. Redis key signals:catalog caches PROPOSED+PROMOTED listing; invalidated synchronously on every promote or archive call — stale-read after any state-mutating call is a defect. Callers of GET /api/signals/catalog must observe updated lifecycle_state immediately after a promote or archive operation completes.
design_contract.public_api: SignalSpecValidator.validate(String yaml): ValidationResult{ok, diagnostics[{fieldPath, errorCode, message, suggestion, file, line}]}; SignalSpecCompiler.compile(ValidatedSpec): FeatureNodeGraph (in-memory only, no Java codegen). REST: POST /api/signals/propose (body: SignalSpec YAML) → ProposalResponse{proposalId, signalId, validationResult}; GET /api/signals/catalog (paginated, filterable by lifecycle_state) → SignalCatalogEntry[]{signalId, author, lifecycle_state, trackRecord}; GET /api/signals/{id} → SignalSpecDetail{full spec + diagnostics + trackRecord}; POST /api/signals/{id}/promote (operator confirmation token required; returns 403 without valid token; returns 422 if signal not in BACKTESTED state; returns 409 on concurrent promote for same signalId) → PromoteResponse; POST /api/signals/{id}/archive → ArchiveResponse. Explainability envelope DTO extended with: author (String), signalId (UUID), signalVersion (Int), proposalId (UUID), trackRecord (TrackRecordSummary).

candidate.problem_statement: There is no declarative signal authoring surface: LLM-proposed SignalSpecs cannot be validated, compiled to FeatureNode graphs, backtested, reviewed, or promoted to live ranking with operator approval and author provenance. The platform cannot close the propose→validate→compile→backtest→promote loop required to make R-016 acceptance criteria reachable.
risk_register: R1 (HIGH): R-015 POST /api/backtest/run not confirmed on main when R-016 impl starts — mitigation: design slice asserts R-015 preflight; impl-primary must not begin until R-015 is confirmed on main.

R2 (HIGH): SignalSpec persistence write path conflicts with Redis+historical-store-only architecture decision — mitigation: design slice adds a repo-memory/DECISIONS.md authorization entry for the QuestDB signal_specs write path before impl-primary begins; reviewer verifies entry exists.

R3 (MEDIUM): platform-dsl/signalspec/ may inadvertently import app-api or app-core classes — mitigation: reviewer import-boundary checklist is a required output of the review slice; build.gradle dependency declarations enforce compile-time module boundaries.

R4 (MEDIUM): Concurrent promote race condition producing duplicate PROMOTED rows — mitigation: lifecycle state CAS at persistence layer; unique constraint on (id, lifecycle_state='PROMOTED') in DDL migration; 409 response wired in SignalController; qa-author includes concurrent-promote test asserting 409.

R5 (MEDIUM): Operator confirmation token bypassable client-side — mitigation: backend always validates token server-side returning 403; SignalApiEndpointTest covers missing-token case before impl-primary lands; reviewer audits Spring Security role annotation and UI confirm-modal wiring.

R6 (MEDIUM): DFS cycle detection may miss indirect cycles of 3+ hops — mitigation: qa-author writes self-ref, 2-hop, and 3-hop cycle fixture cases before impl-primary; reviewer explicitly checks DFS reachability across all transform edges.

R7 (MEDIUM): YAML body stored without re-validation may diverge from validator rules after future schema change — mitigation: re-validate YAML on read per persistence_protocol; GET /api/signals/{id} returns structured invariant-failure error rather than 500; qa-author includes invariant-failure-on-read test case.
R8 (MEDIUM): Explainability envelope extension may break existing api-contract-snapshots tests — mitigation: qa-author updates snapshot fixtures to include new fields before impl-primary lands.

R9 (MEDIUM): specs/SIGNAL_SPEC.md op vocabulary ambiguity in cyclic-transform detection and unknown-ref scoping — mitigation: designer slice resolves all ambiguities in writing and locks the diagnostic schema before qa-author proceeds.
R10 (LOW): YAML injection risk from unsafe YAML constructor — mitigation: SignalSpecValidator must use SnakeYAML SafeConstructor exclusively; reviewer checks for any UnsafeConstructor usage.

R11 (MEDIUM): Redis signals:catalog TTL may serve stale state after promote or archive — mitigation: synchronous Redis key invalidation on every state-mutating call is a hard constraint and documented in design contract; reviewer checks for any code path that exits without invalidation; SignalCatalogStalenessTest in qa-author asserts fresh state is returned immediately after both promote and archive; qa-verify confirms test passes.

R12 (LOW): signal_specs DDL migration absent when integration tests run — mitigation: design contract includes full DDL; impl-primary fails fast if migration file is missing rather than auto-creating tables.
